content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any project documents that specify RPC operating requirements, environmental policy, or prior gas-gap recommendations. Extract the three candidate mixtures, their GWP100 values, and any documented constraints or assumptions relevant to time resolution."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard constraints: discard any candidate mixture with GWP100 greater than 150, and keep only gas gaps in the allowed 1–3 mm range. If no candidate satisfies the GWP100 limit, stop and report that the design constraints are infeasible."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every GWP-compliant candidate mixture, run simulate_time_resolution at a coarse set of gas gaps spanning the allowed range, e.g. 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 mm. Record each numeric time-resolution result with record_results."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best coarse result with the lowest simulated time resolution. Around that mixture and gap, run additional simulations at finer gap values within 1–3 mm, e.g. in 0.1 or 0.2 mm increments around the coarse minimum, and record all numeric results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all compliant simulated configurations and select the mixture and gas gap with the smallest time resolution. Verify again that the chosen mixture is one of the three candidates, has GWP100 no greater than 150, and uses a gap between 1 and 3 mm, then pass these findings to the reporting module for the final recommendation."}]}
